paper.title: Language Models as Zero-Shot Planners: Extracting Actionable Knowledge for Embodied Agents
paper.central_claim: Large pretrained language models contain actionable knowledge for diverse high-level activities without additional domain training; semantic action translation, dynamic example retrieval and interleaved trajectory correction can make their plans executable in embodied environments.
paper.central_claim_son55_wording: Pre-trained LLMs can decompose high-level household tasks into mid-level plans without training; a frozen-model inference procedure (semantic translation to admissible actions + step-wise autoregressive correction + retrieval of the most similar demonstration) raises VirtualHome plan executability from about 18% to 79% at a measurable cost in human-judged correctness.
paper.scope_note: Borderline in scope: frozen LLM planner plus admissible-action projection for a simulated embodied agent; plan is open-loop and the low-level controller is assumed. Kept in scope (interface card K104) as both seats did.

signatures.conditions: 42 atomic actions, allowed object arguments and sufficient semantic embedding similarity.
signatures.feedback: Translated previous actions, not environmental success/failure.
signatures.selection_rule/data: Candidate samples selected by similarity plus beta-scaled mean log probability; epsilon/empty-generation stopping; development settings in Appendix A.1.

signatures.later_use: Fixed components are reused on tasks; within-episode context is read by subsequent planner calls. This is not measured retained self-improvement.
signatures.failure_boundary: Compounded commands, incomplete environment vocabulary and early stopping can preserve validity while losing task correctness.

signatures.object: Planner-LM output stream for VirtualHome: free-form step phrases mapped to the 47,522-step admissible bank (42 atomic actions x allowed arguments)

signatures.output: sequence of admissible actions (executable VirtualHome program)
signatures.conditions: action space enumerable; one instance per object class; low-level controller assumed
signatures.feedback: none from environment; only embedding similarity score
signatures.selection_rule: argmax over a_e of max_a C + beta*P; early termination if best score < epsilon or >50% zero-length samples
signatures.selection_data: no data; epsilon/beta/k/temperature grid-searched on the 88 evaluation tasks (E013, E027)
signatures.persistence: none across tasks; translated actions persist only inside the current prompt
signatures.later_use: conditions later steps of the same plan only
signatures.failure_boundary: compounded instructions mapped poorly; premature termination; expressivity limits of VirtualHome; correctness drop

gap.author_gap: Existing LLM knowledge extraction and language grounding do not yield executable plans for diverse high-level human activities without additional training.
gap.checked_gap: Same-model vanilla generations are often semantically plausible but not executable; projection sharply improves executability while reducing human correctness. The residual is executable-and-correct planning, not merely legal syntax.

gap.residue: Free-form world knowledge does not automatically obey an embodied action vocabulary or preconditions.
gap.stakes: An apparently correct plan cannot be acted on; a merely executable short plan can fail the intended activity.
gap.method_response: Translate to admissible actions, retrieve task-relevant examples and interleave corrected actions into generation.
gap.remaining_gap: No environmental observation/feedback, no physical low-level controller validation, and a substantial correctness/executability tradeoff.

claims.text: Large pretrained language models contain actionable knowledge for diverse high-level activities without additional domain training; semantic action translation, dynamic example retrieval and interleaved trajectory correction can make their plans executable in embodied environments.
claims.setting: Codex12B/GPT-3 175B; 88 activity names, seven VirtualHome scenes; 47,522 allowed action strings.
claims.baseline/control: Vanilla generation; Table 2 component removals; fine-tuned GPT-3 baseline separately.
claims.selection_vs_test: 204 reference tasks; best sampled configuration selected using LCS+executability, independent validation split not established.
claims.result/denominator: Codex executable18.07→78.57%; correctness64.87→54.88%. GPT-3 executable7.79→73.05%; correctness77.86→66.13%. Correctness judged by ten annotators; mean/SEM.
claims.counterevidence: Executable is not equivalent to correct; no observation feedback, and pretrained exposure is unauditable. Ablations report executability/LCS only (no correctness); fine-tuned GPT-3 13B reaches 66.07% executability and higher LCS (34.08) at comparable correctness.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Strong evidence for improving static program executability in this simulator interface, not general autonomous embodied success.

claims.text: Extracted plans contain actionable knowledge rather than merely reproducing valid syntax.
claims.selection_vs_test: Same selected plan outputs, not new independent online test.
claims.result/denominator: Joint correct/executable analysis uses ≥70% annotator approval; human joint reference65.91%.
claims.counterevidence: Some correctness is lost during projection; vocabulary expressivity and early stops remain.
claims.allowed_conclusion: There is a measurable but incomplete bridge from text knowledge to executable activities.

assessment.evidence_level_reason: Open-loop plan generation; executability is a simulator precondition check and correctness is crowd judgment of plan text; no execution-judged task success (EVIDENCE: offline).
assessment.author_claim_kept: Large pretrained language models contain actionable knowledge for diverse high-level activities without additional domain training; semantic action translation, dynamic example retrieval and interleaved trajectory correction can make their plans executable in embodied environments.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: In VirtualHome, frozen Codex 12B / GPT-3 175B with translation, step-wise correction and retrieved examples raise static plan executability (18.07->78.57%, 7.79->73.05%) on 88 task names, at a measured loss of human-judged correctness (64.87->54.88%, 77.86->66.13%), with settings selected on those same tasks. Not closed-loop embodied success.
assessment.reproduction: Author-reported numbers only; nothing run by us.

G.reason: Concrete, sourced bottleneck: vanilla large LMs write plausible but inadmissible plans (GPT-3 175B executability 7.79%, Codex 18.07%); nearest neighbours named (supervised VirtualHome LSTM, concurrent fine-tuned GPT-2) and residue stated (correctness drop, mid-level only, no observation). The supervised comparison is explicitly crude (non-matched split), so neighbour comparison is incomplete. Both seats agree.

M.reason: Translation, step-wise re-conditioning and retrieved examples each target a named failure (inadmissible phrasing, compounded steps, environment conventions) and yield distinguishable predictions (ablation, GloVe vs SBERT). Embedding similarity is a soft proxy for validity and ignores scene state. Both seats agree.

X.reason: Algorithm 1, templates (A.4) and grids (A.1) make the static chain reconstructible; failure boundary explicit (compound instructions, early stop, no observation, assumed controller). Beta/epsilon chosen on the evaluation tasks (handled under E.holdout). Both seats agree.

measurement.reason: Executability is an environment precondition check with full denominators and correctness uses 10 raters with SEM, but neither is closed-loop task success, and each method contributes one selected run per task (single trial, anchors v2: single-trial results cap at 2). Adopt sol over son55's 3.

causality.reason: Fixed-backbone leave-one-out ablation on two planners, Translation-LM swap and program-length control isolate the executability gain; correctness is not measured for ablated variants and each variant is separately tuned on the evaluation tasks. Both seats agree.

holdout.reason: 88 task names are disjoint from the 204-task demonstration bank, but hyperparameters and the best run are selected by LCS+executability on those same 88 tasks; one simulator, no contamination audit. Anchor 2 (development/evaluation overlap). Both seats agree.

statistics.reason: Correctness carries SEM across 10 annotators and vanilla baselines average three prompts; qualitative failure-source analysis (compound instructions, early termination, small-model copying, length control) exists. Executability has no variance/CI and the final method has no repeated trials. Upper edge of the anchor v2 1-2 band. Both seats agree.

cost.reason: Only a qualitative 'minor computation overhead' plus embedding precomputation and sample grids; no calls/tokens/latency. Both seats agree.

reason: Complete fixed package (main text + Appendix A.1-A.5) checked by both seats and the aggregate; all eight ratings resolved under anchors v2.

aggregate_review.initial_evidence_judgment: Read before seat totals: the paper is a frozen-LLM planning procedure for VirtualHome whose only quantitative evidence is plan-level (executability as a precondition check, LCS, crowd correctness). The executability gain is large and ablated; correctness falls; hyperparameters/best runs are selected on the 88 evaluation tasks; no observation or execution feedback; single selected run per method. Expect offline evidence, scoped support, E.measurement capped at 2 by anchors v2, E.holdout at 2.

resolutions.reason: decompose_and_delegate requires routing to a sound solver/checker; the embedding projection is a learned soft mapper with no verification closure. Not a distinct operation the original card describes.

Anchors v2: results that are all single trials cap at 2; one selected plan per task per method; metrics are a static precondition check and crowd text judgment, not execution-judged success. son55's argument that offline-ness belongs only to evidence_level does not override the single-trial cap.
K201 requires an external gate with dispatch/reject feedback; the epsilon threshold is the projection's own similarity score with no state check.

resolutions.sol_value: Large pretrained language models contain actionable knowledge for diverse high-level activities without additional domain training; semantic action translation, dynamic example retrieval and interleaved trajectory correction can make their plans executable in embodied environments.
resolutions.son55_value: Pre-trained LLMs can decompose high-level household tasks into mid-level plans without training; a frozen-model inference procedure (semantic translation to admissible actions + step-wise autoregressive correction + retrieval of the most similar demonstration) raises VirtualHome plan executability from about 18% to 79% at a measurable cost in human-judged correctness.
